plan.name: Meniscus Rehab — 2-Week Introductory Block
plan.description: A 2-week reconditioning starter block for a 36-year-old male recreational lifter recovering from a right medial meniscus tear. Cleared for low-impact strength work. No jumping, no deep knee flexion under load. Prepares the client for progressive loading toward ski-season return.

goals.name: Re-establish lower-body strength
goals.description: Rebuild quad, glute, and hamstring strength through knee-safe ranges of motion to support return to skiing.

milestones.name: Complete all sessions pain-free with RPE ≤ 6

goals.name: Return to skiing next season
goals.description: Build the neuromuscular base and single-leg stability required for safe alpine skiing.

milestones.name: Achieve 30-second single-leg balance on right leg with eyes closed

phases.name: Phase 1 — Tissue Tolerance & Motor Control
phases.description: Establish pain-free movement patterns, activate the VMO and glutes, and build connective tissue tolerance. Knee flexion kept to ≤60° under load. All bilateral lower-body work performed in a partial range.

days.name: Day 1 — Lower Body A (Quad & Glute Focus)

activities.name: Leg Press — Partial ROM (≤60° knee flexion)

days.name: Day 5 — Lower Body B (Hinge & Single-Leg Stability)

activities.name: Single-Leg RDL — Assisted (TRX or Wall Touch)
Low Box Step-Up (20 cm box, bodyweight)
Leg Press — Partial ROM (≤60° knee flexion, +5 kg)

days.name: Day 5 — Lower Body B (Hinge & Single-Leg, Progressive)

activities.name: Single-Leg Balance — Right Leg (Eyes Open, Unstable Surface)
Low Box Step-Up (20 cm, Light DB 5 kg each hand)

checkpoints.name: End of 2-Week Intro Block

measurements.note: Right knee pain/discomfort rating (0–10 NRS) during and after each session
Single-leg balance duration right vs left (seconds)

questions: Any pain or swelling in the right knee during or after sessions?
How does right-leg single-leg balance compare to left?
Is the client ready to progress to Phase 2 accumulation loading?

notifications.message: Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain, locking, or significant swelling in the right knee. Consult your surgeon before continuing.
Keep knee flexion to ≤60° on all loaded lower-body exercises this block. Do not chase depth.
